package dynamoevents

import (
	\"encoding/json\"

func TestFieldsMapRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	original := []byte("'`{"user":"alice","large":9007199254740993,"nested":{"enabled":true,"list":[null,1.25,"value"]},"empty":{}}`)
	item := map[string]*dynamodb.AttributeValue{"Fields": {S: aws.String(string(original))}}
	require.NoError(t, setFieldsMap(item, original))
	require.Nil(t, item["Fields"])
	require.Equal(t, "9007199254740993", aws.StringValue(item[keyFieldsMap].M["large"].N))
	require.NotNil(t, item[keyFieldsMap].M["nested"].M)
	require.NoError(t, restoreFields(item))
	var before, after interface{}
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(original, &before))
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(aws.StringValue(item["Fields"].S)), &after))
	require.Equal(t, before, after)
}

func TestFieldsMapInvalidJSON(t *testing.T) {
	_, err := jsonFieldsMap([]byte(`{"ok":1} broken`))
	require.Error(t, err)
	_, err = jsonFieldsMap([]byte(`[]`))
	require.Error(t, err)
}
EOF

item.text:
DynamoDB event writes now store metadata in the native `FieldsMap` attribute. Event reads still support legacy `Fields` records. A background migration converts existing records in bounded scan pages under a distributed lock, validates their JSON content, and can resume after interruption.

`go test ./lib/events/dynamoevents ./lib/backend` passes. The AWS dependent migration test was added but skipped in this environment.
